stories.headline: Woman stabbed to death at Thornton gas station; suspect arrested on first-degree murder charge
stories.summary:
A 40-year-old woman was fatally stabbed Wednesday afternoon at a Maverick gas station at 237 E. 120th Ave. in Thornton, according to the Thornton Police Department. Officers were already responding to reports of a physical disturbance at the location when the altercation escalated into a stabbing shortly after 5:15 p.m.

Paramedics transported the victim to a hospital, where she later died of her stab wound. The suspect fled the scene before officers arrived, but Anthony Valenta, 28, was arrested later that night after being found driving a vehicle matching the description provided by witnesses.

Valenta was booked into the Adams County Sheriff's Detention Facility at 12:07 a.m. Thursday on suspicion of first-degree murder. Police have not specified whether the suspect and victim were known to each other. The Adams County Coroner's Office will release the victim's identity.

stories.headline: House passes water bill with $208 million for Colorado, including renewed push for Arkansas Valley pipeline
stories.summary:
The U.S. House of Representatives passed the biennial Water Resources Development Act on Wednesday by a vote of 415-9, with all eight Colorado representatives in support. The measure authorizes $208 million in water-related projects and studies for the state through the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers.

The bill includes up to $150 million for rural water projects under a western states program championed by Rep. Brittany Pettersen, a Lakewood Democrat, as well as $22.5 million for northern Front Range and northeastern Colorado water infrastructure, $20 million for Custer County, and $15.6 million for Aurora water and stormwater projects.

Also included is Rep. Lauren Boebert's Finish the Arkansas Valley Conduit Act, which would extend repayment terms and lower the interest rate on a long-sought 130-mile drinking water pipeline serving 39 communities east of Pueblo. President Trump vetoed a previous version of the legislation in December, citing the project's $1.3 billion cost. The Senate has not yet passed its own version of the bill, meaning the two chambers will need to reconcile differences before any measure can reach the president's desk.

stories.headline: Colorado diesel prices reach record $6.04 per gallon, straining food banks, farms and schools
stories.summary:
The average price of diesel fuel in Colorado climbed to a record $6.04 per gallon this week, according to AAA data, surpassing previous highs and sending ripple effects across industries and institutions that depend heavily on the fuel. Food banks, school districts and agricultural operations are among those reporting significant financial strain as a result.

The spike compounds pressure on Colorado's farming sector, where diesel powers equipment essential to harvest operations occurring throughout the fall season. Schools that operate large bus fleets and nonprofit food distributors running refrigerated delivery trucks are also facing sharply higher operating costs.

Regular unleaded gasoline prices in Colorado also rose, averaging $4.37 per gallon statewide according to the latest AAA figures. The dual increases are drawing concern from businesses and public agencies that have limited ability to quickly offset higher fuel costs through their existing budgets.

stories.headline: Denver ownership group under contract to purchase Mercury Cafe building, plans 2027 revival
stories.summary:
A Denver creative events company called CoCreate is under contract to purchase the Mercury Cafe building at 2199 California St., with plans to revive the storied bohemian venue that has been closed since early 2025. Co-CEOs Dante Dunlap and Mitchell Hoverman, along with Director of Experience Jennifer Mosquera, say they intend to restore the original spirit of the space, which founder Marilyn Megenity operated as a hub for poets, musicians and dancers beginning in 1975.

The deal, if completed, would be CoCreate's first real estate acquisition. The group is launching what it described as a "very aggressive" capital raise, though principals declined to disclose the target amount. They also said they are in talks with The Bardo Coffee House to manage morning café operations in the building.

Current owner Danny Newman and his partners purchased the building for $2 million in 2021 with plans to revive the cafe, but health issues, pandemic-era cost increases and a property tax bill that tripled to $60,000 annually led them to close the venue. A subsequent tenant, lesbian bar The Pearl, also closed this spring. The new group expects the deal to close this winter, with a potential reopening in early 2027.

stories.headline: Colorado Startup Week draws more than 10,000 attendees as AI, in-person connection dominate themes
stories.summary:
Colorado Startup Week, now in its 15th year, wrapped up Friday at the renovated former CenturyLink building on 15th Street in Denver, drawing more than 10,000 expected attendees. Organizers deliberately excluded an online participation option, emphasizing the event's mission of fostering direct connections among founders, mentors and investors.

Artificial intelligence surfaced as a dominant topic across sessions throughout the week. But a competing theme — the value of in-person, analog experiences — also drew significant attention, particularly through a session led by Michael Zeisser of Denver investment firm FMZ Ventures, who argued that an emerging "Experience Economy" represents the next major economic sector.

Zeisser's panel included Colorado's current attorney general, a former Denver Broncos player and leaders from the Denver Summit Football Club, the Outside Days festival and mental health company Sondermind. He contended that consumer spending has measurably shifted toward experiences — travel, spectator sports, concerts — since the pandemic, and that Colorado is well-positioned to produce companies that capitalize on the trend.

stories.headline: Bo Nix dismisses panic after Chiefs loss, Marvin Mims sits out practice with foot injury
stories.summary:
Broncos quarterback Bo Nix said Thursday that while Monday night's 31-10 loss to Kansas City was far from acceptable, a film review left him confident there is no need to "freak out" heading into Sunday's home opener against Jacksonville. Nix fumbled three times — losing one — in the season opener, a sharp contrast to his performance over the previous two seasons, but called the turnovers an anomaly he does not expect to repeat.

Nix credited the operation under new offensive coordinator Davis Webb as generally sound despite the lopsided result, pointing instead to individual technique breakdowns as the primary culprit. He said he failed to keep two hands on the ball adequately while in the pocket and after breaking containment before crossing the line of scrimmage.

Wide receiver Marvin Mims Jr. did not practice Thursday due to a foot injury, adding to uncertainty about his availability Sunday. Mims, Denver's All-Pro return specialist, played through a hip issue during the Chiefs game before subsequently being listed on the injury report with the foot. Head coach Sean Payton declined to say whether Mims is at risk of missing the Jacksonville game.

stories.headline: Tim Tebow to return to Empower Field for first time since 2012 Broncos home opener Sunday
stories.summary:
Former Broncos quarterback Tim Tebow will return to Empower Field at Mile High on Sunday for Denver's home opener against Jacksonville, participating in the pregame tradition of planting the club's alumni flag. It will be Tebow's first appearance at the stadium since Jan. 8, 2012, when he threw an overtime touchdown pass to Demaryius Thomas to defeat Pittsburgh in a Wild Card playoff game.

Tebow went 8-8 as Denver's starter in the 2011 regular season before Peyton Manning's signing led to his trade to the New York Jets. He made a brief return attempt as a tight end with Jacksonville in 2021 but did not make the team's final roster. He has since focused primarily on broadcasting and other endeavors.

Current Broncos quarterback Bo Nix, who said Tebow was his favorite player growing up and that the two have developed a friendship since Nix was drafted, called the occasion "awesome." Several other Broncos players also cited Tebow as an influential figure from their childhoods, including receiver Pat Bryant, who grew up a Florida Gators fan in Jacksonville.

stories.headline: Avalanche goalie Mackenzie Blackwood opens training camp motivated after inconsistent 2025-26 season
stories.summary:
Colorado Avalanche goaltender Mackenzie Blackwood opened training camp Thursday with a renewed sense of purpose after what he described as a personally disappointing 2025-26 season, despite the Avalanche's Jennings Trophy win for fewest goals allowed. Blackwood was largely overshadowed by tandem partner Scott Wedgewood, who led the NHL in goals-against average and save percentage.

Blackwood missed the start of last season while rehabbing an injury and was unable to train normally over the preceding offseason. He ultimately went 13-1-1 with a .924 save percentage through the end of 2025 but struggled with consistency in the new year, missed additional time in January and was relegated to a backup role for much of the playoffs. He also narrowly missed Canada's 2026 Winter Olympics roster.

Head coach Jared Bednar said Blackwood had an "incredible offseason" and arrived at camp in the best shape of his life, adding that his goal is to use Blackwood as the team's primary starter if the goalie performs as expected. Blackwood said his motivation is clear: "I didn't go home and feel satisfied or proud of the year, that's for sure."

stories.headline: Kitchen fire damages Congress Park's Kabob House restaurant; one employee treated for smoke inhalation
stories.summary:
A stove fire at Kabob House, a Persian restaurant at 825 N. Colorado Blvd. in Denver's Congress Park neighborhood, burned through the roof Wednesday afternoon, according to Denver Fire Department officials. Crews responded at 4:31 p.m. after reports of heavy smoke coming from the roof of the commercial building.

Firefighters found the stove ablaze in the kitchen, with flames extending through the exhaust hood and into the roof structure. Crews extinguished both the kitchen and roof fires, which the department said it "aggressively attacked." One restaurant employee was treated by paramedics for smoke inhalation.

Kabob House is owned and operated by siblings Reza and Nadia Ahmadi, who built the restaurant around their grandmother's recipes. The extent of damage and the restaurant's timeline for reopening were not immediately available.

stories.headline: Showers and storms to persist through weekend; Saturday brings greatest flood risk for Colorado plains
stories.summary:
An unsettled weather pattern will continue across Colorado through the weekend, with scattered afternoon and evening showers and thunderstorms expected to affect both the Front Range and the eastern plains. A Flood Watch remained in effect through midnight Thursday for southwest Colorado near Telluride, and forecasters warned of possible minor flooding and rockslides in the mountains.

Friday is expected to bring another round of scattered afternoon and evening thunderstorms developing over the mountains before moving toward the Interstate 25 corridor and plains, with above-normal moisture keeping heavy rain the primary concern. Highs are expected in the low to mid-80s. Saturday is forecast to be the most active day, with more widespread storms and the greatest potential for localized flooding, particularly across the northeastern plains Saturday night.

Temperatures will drop noticeably over the weekend, with highs mainly in the 70s Saturday and Sunday. Conditions are expected to improve by Monday as a weak ridge of high pressure moves in, though forecasters note another unsettled period may develop mid-week.

stories.headline: Eastern Colorado's World's Wonder View Tower marks 100th anniversary with artist renovation, Saturday celebration
stories.summary:
The World's Wonder View Tower in Genoa, a Ripley's Believe It or Not! roadside attraction located about 100 miles southeast of Denver along Interstate 70, is celebrating its 100th anniversary Saturday with an artist reception beginning at noon. The tower, which claims to offer views of six states from its summit, has undergone a significant renovation led by the Friends of the Genoa Tower nonprofit, which was formed in 2020 after the site fell into disrepair following longtime owner Jerry Chubbuck's death in 2013.

Four Denver artists — Phil Bender, Mark Friday, Lonnie Hanzon and Deborah Jang — each took over one of the tower's four floors to create a vertical museum experience. The exterior has been repainted in gray, maroon and tangerine colors reminiscent of its 1960s appearance. Some of Chubbuck's original curiosities, including a mummified cat and a jackalope, remain on display in the gift shop.

The 153-person town of Genoa sits in Lincoln County on the Eastern Plains. The nonprofit's preservation effort is being carried out in three phases; the crumbling row of wood and stone buildings at the tower's base, which once housed a café, theater and museum, awaits restoration in later phases of the project.

stories.headline: Six Aurora teens to face charges following August 'teen takeover' near Del Mar Park
stories.summary:
Six Aurora teenagers will face charges stemming from a large gathering in August near Del Mar Park that was described by authorities as a "teen takeover," according to officials. The incident drew significant public attention and prompted a law enforcement response in the Aurora area.

Details of the specific charges were not immediately available, but the case has been under investigation since the August event. Aurora authorities have been working to identify participants and build cases against those alleged to have committed criminal acts during the gathering.

The incident added to ongoing discussions in the Aurora metro area about public safety and youth-related disturbances. The case will proceed through the juvenile justice system given the ages of those charged.

topStory.headline: Polish PM warns Russia planning 'accidental' drone and missile strikes on NATO allies supporting Ukraine
topStory.summary:
Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk warned the Polish parliament Thursday that intelligence assessments show Russia is planning hybrid strikes using drones and missiles against European countries supporting Ukraine, including Poland. Tusk described the intelligence as "very consistent and convincing," saying Moscow intends to disguise the attacks as accidental in order to undermine NATO's willingness to invoke collective defense obligations under Article 5 of the alliance's founding treaty.

Tusk said Russia's strategy is to use recurring incidents to portray NATO as incapable of a unified response, eroding confidence in the alliance's mutual defense commitments. "The aim will be to weaken NATO's integrity in general and, above all, to convince member states that Article 5 is more theoretical than practical — that is, the assumption that no one will want to die for Latvia or Lithuania," Tusk said, warning that each staged accident would serve as an escalating demonstration of NATO's perceived helplessness.

The warning came as a drone struck a petrol station near Ukraine's border with Poland on Thursday, and Polish air defenses were activated after a jet-powered drone approached Polish airspace before exploding approximately four kilometers from the border. Airports in Lublin and Rzeszow temporarily suspended operations as a precaution. The incidents followed a Russian drone strike on a train near the Polish-Ukrainian border the previous Sunday, during which several European leaders were in transit through the area.

Tusk announced he would travel overnight to Kyiv, arriving Friday, for talks with Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy on defenses against new drone types and additional sanctions against Russia. He also said Russia is not prepared for any peace negotiations short of Ukraine's "total capitulation" and that Moscow believes the coming winter will be "tragically critical" for Ukraine, with intelligence indicating high-frequency, high-intensity attacks on six major Ukrainian cities are expected in the near term. Slovak Prime Minister Robert Fico, who has maintained warmer ties with Moscow while criticizing Western military aid to Ukraine, also said he would be in Kyiv, as the European Union announced it would disburse 3.3 billion euros to Ukraine on Friday to purchase missiles and drones.
